name: Alkarab
description: A star 52 parsecs away, 5.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: radius 5.711 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 37.449 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.043) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: effective temperature 5979 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.053)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: distance 52.247 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 52 parsecs away, 5.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 37 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,979 K, so 5.711 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 115623: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Upsilon Pegasi
quotes.card: Upsilon Pegasi, Latinised from υ Pegasi, is a star within the great square in the northern constellation of Pegasus.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Alkarab.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2839853133694170880 (quality B), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
